annotations.title: Heat index and heat illness trigger check

description: Compute the NWS heat index from temperature and humidity and check it against California, Oregon or Maryland heat-illness triggers, or your own, for one reading or an hourly log. Use this tested BusCalc worksheet when the task matches its inputs and scope. Returns named results, units, formula, assumptions, method version, reference-value notes (official figure or your figure, with source and effective date), a check link and a source-page URL. Official reference values are prefilled when omitted; supply every other figure from the user's records. Percent fields take percent numbers. No figures are looked up; no private projects or purchases are accessed. Put tool fields inside inputs. Supply units or modelVersion only when listed in inputSchema. Follow its required fields and exact choices. Do not pass the REST calculator field inside MCP arguments.

caHigh.description: California: high-heat procedures when temperature equals or exceeds (°F). Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for california: high-heat procedures when temperature equals or exceeds. Unknown is not the same as zero. Official reference value 95 °F from Cal. Code Regs. tit. 8, §3395(e) (Cal/OSHA), effective current text viewed 2026-11-09. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used. Used only when rule is ca; ignored otherwise.

caShade.description: California: shade required when temperature exceeds (°F). Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for california: shade required when temperature exceeds. Unknown is not the same as zero. Official reference value 80 °F from Cal. Code Regs. tit. 8, §3395(d)(1) (Cal/OSHA), effective current text viewed 2026-11-09. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used. Used only when rule is ca; ignored otherwise.

entry.description: Reading entered as. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for reading entered as. Unknown is not the same as zero. Used only when mode is single; ignored otherwise. Options: trh = Air temperature and relative humidity; hi = Heat index entered directly.

hiDirect.description: Heat index (°F). Heat index from the NWS or the OSHA-NIOSH Heat Safety Tool. Used only when mode is single and entry is hi; ignored otherwise.

mdHigh.description: Maryland: high-heat procedures when heat index equals or exceeds (°F). Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for maryland: high-heat procedures when heat index equals or exceeds. Unknown is not the same as zero. Official reference value 90 °F from COMAR 09.12.32.08A (Maryland heat stress standards), effective current COMAR text viewed 2026-11-09. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used. Used only when rule is md; ignored otherwise.

mdScope.description: Maryland: heat stress standard applies when heat index equals or exceeds (°F). Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for maryland: heat stress standard applies when heat index equals or exceeds. Unknown is not the same as zero. Official reference value 80 °F from COMAR 09.12.32.02A (Maryland heat stress standards), effective current COMAR text viewed 2026-11-09. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used. Used only when rule is md; ignored otherwise.

mdTop.description: Maryland: 15-minute hourly rest when heat index is above (°F). Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for maryland: 15-minute hourly rest when heat index is above. Unknown is not the same as zero. Official reference value 100 °F from COMAR 09.12.32.08C(1)(b) (Maryland heat stress standards), effective current COMAR text viewed 2026-11-09. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used. Used only when rule is md; ignored otherwise.

mode.description: Calculation mode. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for calculation mode. Unknown is not the same as zero. Options: single = One reading; log = Hourly log of readings.

orHigh.description: Oregon: high-heat rest breaks when heat index equals or exceeds (°F). Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for oregon: high-heat rest breaks when heat index equals or exceeds. Unknown is not the same as zero. Official reference value 90 °F from OAR 437-002-0156(5)(e) Table 1 (Oregon OSHA), effective 2022-06-15. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used. Used only when rule is or; ignored otherwise.

orShade.description: Oregon: shade and water when heat index equals or exceeds (°F). Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for oregon: shade and water when heat index equals or exceeds. Unknown is not the same as zero. Official reference value 80 °F from OAR 437-002-0156(1), (3) (Oregon OSHA), effective 2022-06-15. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used. Used only when rule is or; ignored otherwise.

orTop.description: Oregon: longer rest breaks when heat index equals or exceeds (°F). Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for oregon: longer rest breaks when heat index equals or exceeds. Unknown is not the same as zero. Official reference value 100 °F from OAR 437-002-0156(5)(e) Table 1 (Oregon OSHA), effective 2022-06-15. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used. Used only when rule is or; ignored otherwise.

ownBasis.description: Your trigger is measured as. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for your trigger is measured as. Unknown is not the same as zero. Used only when rule is own; ignored otherwise. Options: hi = Heat index; temp = Air temperature.

ownHigh.description: Your high-heat trigger (your figure) (°F). Enter the high-heat trigger from the rule or policy you follow; the example is illustrative. Used only when rule is own; ignored otherwise.

ownLow.description: Your first trigger (your figure) (°F). Enter the trigger from the rule or policy you follow; the example is illustrative. Used only when rule is own; ignored otherwise.

readings.description: Hourly readings. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for hourly readings. Unknown is not the same as zero. Used only when mode is log; ignored otherwise.

hour.description: Hour of day (0–23) (h). Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for hour of day (0–23). Unknown is not the same as zero.

rh.description: Relative humidity. Enter as a percent number. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for relative humidity. Unknown is not the same as zero.

tempF.description: Air temperature (dry bulb) (°F). For California, the dry-bulb temperature measured in the unshaded work area with the sensor shielded from direct sunlight (§3395(b)).

rh.description: Relative humidity. Enter as a percent number. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for relative humidity. Unknown is not the same as zero. Used only when mode is single and entry is trh; ignored otherwise.

rule.description: State rule to check. Use matching records or an explicitly identified assumption for state rule to check. Unknown is not the same as zero. Options: ca = California outdoor (Title 8 §3395, air temperature); or = Oregon (OAR 437-002-0156, heat index); md = Maryland (COMAR 09.12.32, heat index); own = Enter your own trigger (for example Washington or Nevada).

tempF.description: Air temperature (dry bulb) (°F). For California, §3395(b) uses the dry-bulb temperature measured in the unshaded work area, with the thermometer bulb or sensor shielded from direct sunlight. For the heat index (Oregon, Maryland), use the air temperature from a thermometer or weather observation at the work area. Used only when mode is single and entry is trh; ignored otherwise.

modelVersion.description: Optional expected method version; a mismatch is rejected.

notes.description: Reference-value notes first, then model notes and the standard limit statement.

referenceValues.description: One entry per official reference value in play: the official figure, the figure used, status official or user, source, effective date and the note text.
